examples.knowledge_point: The Second Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
examples.problem: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \langle t^6,\, t^5\rangle,$ Calculate $\mathbf r''(t).$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t) = t^6,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =6{t}^{5} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =30{t}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t) = t^5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =5{t}^{4} \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =20{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨30{t}^{4},\,20{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =10⟨3{t}^{4},\,2{t}^{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the derivative of  $f(t)=\operatorname{arccos}⁡3t\,i-5{t}^{4}\,j+\frac{2}{{t}^{3}}\,k$ with respect to $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We find the derivative of $f(t)$  by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡3t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{4})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{3}})\,k \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{1-9{t}^{2}}}\,i-20{t}^{3}\,j-\frac{6}{{t}^{4}}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
